trust_decision.summary: The proxy trusts any browser Origin on a WebSocket upgrade: whether the handshake is accepted and relayed upstream is decided only in handle_openai_responses_ws, which copies the client handshake headers verbatim and never inspects Origin, while the HTTP path already restricts origins to loopback (CORS) and the HTTP handlers never reach this code.

landing_point.why: The summary says Cross-Site WebSocket Hijacking, and handle_openai_responses_ws is the only server-side WebSocket handler in the Python proxy; an engineer reads the handshake block at openai.py:3573-3579 and adds the check there.

fix_sites.module_kind: helper block in a route handler module (headroom/proxy/handlers/openai.py)

O3_reason_to_dismiss: The Rust headroom-proxy is a separate binary crate described as a Phase-1 transparent passthrough that only forwards traffic verbatim, and the advisory plus its fix are entirely Python (headroom/proxy), so a solver can call it a different product whose origin policy was never in scope.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: Native CLI clients (Codex declares supports_websockets=true and sends no Origin) and local dashboards on arbitrary loopback ports must keep connecting; an over-broad fix that requires an Origin, or exact-matches HEADROOM_CORS_ORIGINS, locks both out. The published fix documents the exception at fix.diff:71-77 (absence allowed, loopback origins allowed by default).

O6_input_shapes: no Origin header at all (native client) -> allowed
ordinary remote https origin (https://remote.example) -> denied by default
loopback origins http://localhost:3000 and https://127.0.0.1:8787 -> allowed by default
origin with scheme ws/wss or http/https, upper-case host name
explicit default port (:80 for http/ws, :443 for https/wss) normalised away, non-default port kept
origin with a path or trailing slash normalised to scheme://host[:port]
opaque origin 'null' (sandboxed iframe / file://) -> denied as an unparseable scheme/host
header name in mixed case (case-insensitive _header_get over a plain dict)
HEADROOM_WS_ORIGINS allowlist: single value, comma-separated list, '*' wildcard, and fallback to HEADROOM_CORS_ORIGINS

O8_uncovered_routes.route: The Rust reverse proxy accepts a WebSocket upgrade on any path via its catch-all and relays it with the browser's Origin and Authorization headers, with no Origin validation anywhere in the crate
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: Separate Rust crate, described as a 'transparent passthrough' that runs in front of the Python proxy, so a solver argues the origin policy belongs to the Python layer it forwards to
O8_uncovered_routes.distance: different language and build (cargo crate, no Python imports); RUST_DEV.md:45-49 says it is meant to sit on the public port in front of the Python proxy

O8b_injection_room.sibling: a fifth WebSocket alias route (e.g. /v1/codex/{sub}/responses or a provider-prefixed /openai/v1/responses) registered next to the existing four
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: The maintainer has already added four near-identical aliases over time (/v1/responses, /v1/codex/responses, /backend-api/responses, /backend-api/codex/responses); one more added for a new client would be forgotten if the guard were written per-route instead of in the shared handler.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: a Rust-side origin allowlist in ws_handler's pre-upgrade path (inspect the Origin header before ws.on_upgrade)
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: The Rust proxy is the documented public-port front end and mirrors Python behaviour elsewhere (header stripping, internal-header policy), so a maintainer porting the fix would naturally add the same gate there.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: the same origin gate applied to a second accept/relay shape, e.g. an HTTP-POST-to-WebSocket bridge or a re-handshake path that bypasses the shared pre-accept block
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: The module already carries a WS->HTTP fallback that re-serialises the first frame and re-issues the request; a maintainer adding a reciprocal HTTP->WS relay would reuse ws_headers without passing through the new pre-accept check.

O9_family: Cross-site WebSocket hijacking: missing Origin validation on a local proxy's WebSocket upgrade (CWE-1385, CWE-287)

O10_build.language: Python (proxy/CLI) plus a Rust workspace (headroom-core, headroom-proxy, headroom-py, headroom-parity)
O10_build.toolchain: maturin + pip for the wheel, cargo 1.80 for the crates, pytest/anyio for Python tests, cargo test for Rust

j.j_tempting_wrong_fix: Add a raw-string Origin allowlist inside handle_openai_responses_ws only, rejecting requests with no Origin (breaking native Codex) and leaving the Rust headroom-proxy WebSocket handler untouched.

unverified: repo_mb: no shell available, so size was not measured; the tree has ~3400 tracked files plus a Rust workspace, clearly above 5 MB and well below 1.5 GB.

Whether an operator running the Rust headroom-proxy alone (upstream = api.openai.com) would have proxy-side credentials injected for a WebSocket: websocket.rs forwards the client's Authorization and injects none, so the credential part of the hijack is deployment-dependent; the missing Origin gate itself is certain.
Latest release code was not provided (latest: none), so present_in_latest for the Rust route stays unknown.

The pinned tree already defines a case-insensitive _header_get in headroom/proxy/auth_mode.py:72-79; the fix re-implements it locally in openai.py instead of importing it. Whether that duplication is deliberate was not verified.

headroom/proxy/loopback_guard.py:28 still documents a wide-open CORS policy (allow_origins=['*']) although headroom/proxy/server.py:2305-2320 already restricts it to a loopback regex; treated as a stale docstring, not pursued.
